## About "Hydras of the World"

The main objective of this project is to provide a resource for people interested in the kinds of hydra that inhabit the world. It seems to me that understanding the diversity of hydra species in an evolutionary framework is essential for scientists working with hydra.  Biology research has made important progress by studying **model organisms** to understand fundamental biological processes. But research that is overwhelmingly skewed toward a tiny handful of species creates a severely distorted view of life (a taxomic bias). Hydra biologists like to say that we study a "non-model organism", but then we generalized our findings based on studies of a single laboratory strain—sometimes of somewhat unknown origen (see lab strains). Variation is the norm not the exception. I am hopeful that this pages will encourage my colleagues to characterize taxonomically the strains they are studying. There is evidence that the laboratory strains that we use (e.g. H. vulgaris 105, H. vulgaris AEP) have "evolved" since they were collected . This is expected given that 105 and AEP have been in different labs around the world for more than 40 and 30 years. Once cna imagine the culture passing through regular bottlenecks and undergoing regular selection.
